outcomeNote: a mishna recording three tannaitic positions; the gemara takes them up in the following units

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַגּוֹסֵס וְהַיּוֹצֵא לֵיהָרֵג — לֹא נִידָּר וְלֹא נֶעֱרָךְ. רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא אוֹמֵר: נֶעֱרָךְ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁדָּמָיו קְצוּבִין. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: נוֹדֵר וּמַעֲרִיךְ וּמַקְדִּישׁ, וְאִם הִזִּיק — חַיָּיב.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «One who is moribund and one who is taken to be executed» after being sentenced by the court «is neither» the object of «a vow nor valuated. Rabbi Ḥanina ben Akavya says:» He is not the object of a vow, because he has no market value; but «he is valuated, due to» the fact «that one’s value is fixed» by the Torah based on age and sex. «Rabbi Yosei says:» One with that status «vows» to donate the assessment of another person to the Temple treasury, «and takes» vows of «valuation, and consecrates» his property; «and if he damages» the property of others, he is «liable» to pay compensation.

moves.cueHe: הגוסס והיוצא ליהרג — לא נידר ולא נערך
moves.summary: the anonymous mishna rules that neither is the object of a vow of assessment nor valuated
moves.about: whether one who is being taken out to be executed is subject to valuation (erekh), given that a person's valuation is fixed by the Torah and does not depend on market value

moves.summary: R' Hanina ben Akavya holds he is valuated, since valuations are fixed by the Torah
moves.about: whether a moribund man or one taken out to be executed remains competent to vow another's assessment, to take vows of valuation, to consecrate his property and to be liable for damage he causes

moves.summary: R' Yosei holds such a person still vows, valuates, consecrates, and is liable for damage

edges.cueHe: רבי חנינא בן עקביא אומר: נערך, מפני שדמיו קצובין
edges.about: whether one who is being taken out to be executed is subject to valuation (erekh), given that a person's valuation is fixed by the Torah and does not depend on market value

edges.cueHe: רבי יוסי אומר: נודר ומעריך ומקדיש, ואם הזיק — חייב
edges.about: whether a moribund man or one taken out to be executed remains competent to vow another's assessment, to take vows of valuation, to consecrate his property and to be liable for damage he causes
